applicant_utility.summary: The stipend is 48,000 yen per month at undergraduate/graduate level (30,000 yen at Japanese language institutes), paid for either 12 months from April or 6 months from October, and it is a living-cost stipend only. You cannot apply directly to JASSO: your school nominates you within a quota that depends on how many international students it enrolls, so the first step is your international student office. The grant is blocked if you hold a MEXT or foreign government scholarship, receive other allowances averaging over 90,000 yen a month (excluding tuition/enrollment fee), have a Japan-based supporter earning 5 million yen or more a year, or also draw on the JASSO Student Exchange Support Program. Keep the language evidence ready (JLPT N2+, EJU Japanese 200+, or B2 CEFR English) unless you study at a Japanese-language or preparatory programme, which is exempt.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Privately-financed students already enrolled in Japan who can survive a competitive, institution-gated nomination and need monthly living support rather than tuition.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm with your school's international student office that it nominates students for this scholarship, and obtain its current application guidelines and the number of recommendation slots.
Identify which window your school nominates for (12 months from April or 6 months from October) so you apply in the round that matches your enrolment stage.

Gather the supporter's income certificate if you have a financial supporter in Japan, and total your other allowances to check the 90,000 yen-per-month average cap (tuition and enrollment fee excluded).
Verify your language evidence (JLPT N2+, EJU Japanese 200+ in Japanese as a Foreign Language, or B2 CEFR English) if you are not at an exempt Japanese-language or preparatory programme.
common_rejection_risks: Your institution fills its recommendation quota with higher-graded students, or your institution does not nominate at all for this scholarship.
Failing the grading criteria set out in the current year's application guidelines.
Other allowances (excluding tuition and enrollment fee) averaging more than 90,000 yen per month, or a Japan-based financial supporter with annual income of 5 million yen or more.
Holding a MEXT scholarship, a foreign government scholarship, or the JASSO Student Exchange Support Program, all of which bar an award.
Not meeting the Japanese/English language condition at a non-exempt institution type.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Enrollment and tuition fees, international airfare, visa and travel costs, health-insurance costs, and any accommodation or living expenses beyond what the 48,000 yen monthly stipend covers.
applicant_utility.document_audit: The official English page publishes no document list, so every form comes from your institution's guidelines; obtain the current application guidelines and form directly from the international student office rather than reusing a previous round's paperwork or forms from another school.
alerts: Institutions that have suspended this scholarship are listed on the official page (currently none), but you must confirm your own school participates before planning around the grant.
Grant recipients must sign the JASSO-designated sheet every month at the international students' office and must agree to cooperate with JASSO's career path survey after the award.
The 2026 selection results were published on 5 June 2026; if you missed that round, ask your school about the 6-month October intake instead.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You submit nothing to JASSO yourself: your institution screens and recommends you, JASSO makes the award decision for the institution's designated round, and payments follow the institution's schedule.

applicant_utility.summary: This is JASSO's stipend for short-term exchange students (8 days to one year) studying at a Japanese university under an exchange agreement with their home institution, paid as a flat 80,000 yen per month. You can never apply directly: only the Japanese host university can submit the scholarship application to JASSO, and the selection method differs from school to school, so your starting point is your home school's exchange office. The award only fits you if your total scholarship income for study in Japan stays at or below 80,000 yen a month and you will return to your home institution after the programme.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Exchange students on active partner agreements who need monthly living support for a stay of 8 days to one year and have no other Japan-study scholarship stacked on top.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your home school has an exchange agreement or arrangement with the specific Japanese school and that your programme runs between 8 days and one year.
Ask the home school how the host university screens and nominates exchange students for this stipend, since JASSO accepts applications only from the Japanese school.
Total every other scholarship or allowance for study in Japan and confirm the combined monthly amount does not exceed 80,000 yen.
Match your stay length to the visa rule: 90 days or less means the Japanese school arranges your status of residence, while longer stays require 'Student' visa eligibility.
common_rejection_risks: No exchange agreement between your home school and the Japanese school, or the Japanese school does not nominate exchange students.
Combined scholarships for study in Japan above 80,000 yen per month, which makes you ineligible regardless of need.
You cannot show that you will return to your home school and complete your studies there after the Japanese programme.
Missing the host school's exchange window, because students must start within the school's designated period and selection timing is school-specific.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Any tuition charged by the Japanese school, international airfare, accommodation beyond the 80,000 yen monthly stipend, insurance, and other day-to-day living costs.
applicant_utility.document_audit: JASSO's English page lists no documents, so the paperwork is defined by your home school and the host university; the one document-point that matters is clear proof of acceptance under the exchange agreement, which is what the host school attaches when nominating you.
alerts: Applications are accepted only from the Japanese school, so no amount of direct contact with JASSO will get you funded.
Students from Taiwan and Palestine are acceptable even though the rule is phrased as countries with diplomatic relations with Japan.
The official page is dated 'As of January 31, 2024'; confirm the current terms and amount with the host university before relying on this page.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to the exchange programme through your home school; the Japanese host university screens and submits the scholarship application to JASSO, which decides which programmes to support.
